title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 173 (Meetings of the board)

content.overview: Section 173 requires the first board meeting within thirty days of incorporation and at least four meetings every year, with not more than 120 days between meetings.
content.glance: Section 173 requires the first board meeting within thirty days of incorporation and at least four meetings every year, with not more than 120 days between meetings.
content.study: Notice of not less than seven days must be given in writing to every director at the Indian address, and by hand, post or electronic means. A shorter notice is allowed for urgent business if at least one independent director, where the company has one, is present or ratifies. Participation by video conferencing is permitted except for matters the rules restrict from being dealt with by video, unless the rules in force allow them. OPC, small company, dormant company and private start-up exemptions on frequency must be checked from the notification in force rather than assumed. Quorum is s. 174, not s. 173.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can the board meet only twice because business is quiet?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Not unless an exemption notification applies. The default is four meetings and a 120-day gap.

caseLaw.point: A company holds at least four board meetings in a year, with not more than one hundred and twenty days between meetings, subject to the one person company relaxation. This is a statutory pointer, not a judgment.
